value.title: Cross-model review r3 (final) — omp-statusline-name
value.note: Scoped re-review of the post-r2 delta only, on the current working tree. Read-only throughout; no source or test mutated. Re-derived by me: targeted `npx vitest run core/session-name.test.ts index.test.ts` bare exit 0, 23/23 (6 + 17); `just typecheck` exit 0; standalone `core/worktree.test.ts` exit 0, 7/7. My own full `harness checks` went red on the SAME unrelated worktree.test.ts tmpdir teardown race as in r1 (different case in the same file) — see V3-GATE, where I compose that against the PM's green and against file mtimes. FINAL VERDICT: APPROVE FOR PR. All five r2 items are discharged. CLOSED OUT 2026-09-02: the last NIT (P-1) was fixed in place with the exact converse assertion I specified, verified by me, and no round 4 was opened.

value.finding: The recovery notice is now witnessed; its SUPPRESSION guard still is not. index.test.ts:288 proves the recovery line appears after a warning, in order. Nothing proves the converse — that a session which never warned gets NO `set after retry` line. The nearest test, :270 'reasserts immediately on the first turn when startup publication missed', filters only for `could not set omp session name` and asserts that absent, so a spurious info notice would pass it silently. This is the same shape as N-1 one level down, and I am recording it as a NIT rather than reopening: the failure mode is one extra info line on a session that recovered inside its window, the guard is two tokens and visible on the same screen as its only caller, and the marginal value of a fourth round is below its cost. SMALLEST FIX, if you are touching the file anyway: widen :270's existing filter from `could not set omp session name` to `omp session name` and assert the result is the empty array — one word changed, and it closes the converse.
value.receipt: index.test.ts:283 now filters every `omp session name` notice and asserts []; targeted suite re-run by me at 23/23, bare exit 0.
value.note: CLOSED 2026-09-02. The PM applied the one-word fix verbatim: index.test.ts:283 in 'reasserts immediately on the first turn when startup publication missed' went from `.some(m => m.includes("could not set omp session name"))` asserted false, to `.filter(m => m.includes("omp session name"))` asserted `[]`. Verified non-vacuous by inspection: that test's fake takes on attempt 2, so the reassert lands at turn_start and the primary's 250ms readback then matches — delete the `if (state.noticeShown)` suppression guard and notifyRecovered fires into a session that never warned, the filter returns one entry, and the assertion fails. The converse is now witnessed, which is what P-1 asked for.

value.rationale: N-1 CLOSED, and the test is better than the one I specified. index.test.ts:288 'announces recovery when the first turn succeeds after the retry notice' drives the real production sequence under fake timers: `sessionNameTakesAfter = 6` so all five scheduled attempts miss, `advanceTimersByTimeAsync(10_000)` exhausts the window, then it asserts sessionNames is 5 and that the filtered notice list EQUALS exactly one `could not set` entry — which incidentally also witnesses G3's exactly-once and the absence of a premature recovery line. turn_start then produces the sixth set and, after a microtask flush, the filtered list EQUALS the two lines IN ORDER. Non-vacuous by inspection: delete the notifyRecovered() call and the second array assertion fails. Mock hygiene checked and clean — `vi.useRealTimers()` in a finally, `vi.restoreAllMocks()` in the suite afterEach, so the fake-timer block cannot leak into the sibling tests I was worried about. Residue P-1 is the converse guard.

N-2 CLOSED. The test is renamed 'does not reassert after startup publication has SETTLED successfully', which is exactly the wire fact it establishes rather than the broader claim its old name made. The in-flight-but-destined-to-succeed case remains uncovered and remains a non-defect: G1 licenses one extra attempt on the first user turn and the set is idempotent. Naming it honestly was the whole ask.

N-3 ACCEPTED AS DELIBERATE. Blind mode runs its bounded schedule to completion rather than early-exiting on first success; the PM records this as intentional and production-unreachable, which matches the tree — impl-guide risk r1 is RESOLVED with the ExtensionAPI citation, and index.ts always supplies getSessionName. A deliberate bounded choice on a dead path needs no change; my r2 note was tidiness and I am withdrawing it rather than carrying it forward.

N-4 CLOSED. AC4's receipt now reads 'Final-tree harness checks status ok at 2026-09-01T22:48:46.093Z; all eight sensors passed', and AC3's was refreshed to 6/6 and 17/17 alongside it. I checked the receipt actually covers the tree rather than taking the timestamp on trust: every product file's mtime is at or before 22:44:18Z (index.ts 22:44:18Z, index.test.ts 22:44:00Z, session-name.ts 22:27:03Z, session-name.test.ts 22:27:23Z), all earlier than the 22:48:46Z run. The receipt is honest.

N-5 CLOSED, and fixed at the root rather than worked around. `const state = { reasserted, took, noticeShown }` is preallocated BEFORE deps, so the `notice` closure captures an initialised object instead of a temporal-dead-zone binding; `notifyRecovered` now closes over `generation`, `ctx` and `name` only and holds no reference to `publication` at all; and `publication` itself is a `const` initialised at its declaration. The class of bug is gone, not merely unreachable. `notifyRecovered` also gained its own try/catch, so an unavailable notice surface cannot turn a successful recovery into a rejection — consistent with the containment R-06 established across the helper.

GATE — two honest runs that disagree, composed rather than reported one-sided. The PM's final-tree `harness checks` at 22:48:46Z is green on all eight sensors, and the mtime check above proves it covers this tree. My own `harness checks` on the same tree went RED: seven sensors pass, `test` fails in core/worktree.test.ts afterEach with `ENOTEMPTY, Directory not empty: /var/folders/.../pij-worktree-QW1ZAJ`. This is the SECOND occurrence on my seat, in a different case of the same file as the r1 red ('verify refuses a branch or SHA mismatch' now, 'creates from a base SHA resolved at create-time' then), and it is a teardown race in a file plan 125 does not touch: `rmSync` on a tmpdir racing whatever is still holding it. Re-running that file standalone is exit 0, 7/7, as it was in r1. My reading: an environmental flake local to my seat, not a defect and not a reason to withhold approval — but it belongs in the record as harness friction with a real repro rate rather than being quietly dropped because the PM's run was green. It is also the second sensor-level instance of the family the packet already lists as known-open (i8 / DL-002), which is now enough of a pattern to be worth a harness observation of its own: the cleanup should tolerate ENOTEMPTY (retry, or `force` with a retry loop) rather than failing the whole gate. FINAL VERDICT: APPROVE FOR PR. All four ACs true, all seven r1 findings and all five r2 items discharged, and P-1 now closed too. FINAL RECEIPTS, re-derived by me after the P-1 edit: targeted suite bare exit 0 at 23/23; AC4 cites the ship gate at 2026-09-01T23:04:10.350Z with all eight sensors green, and I checked that run covers the edited tree rather than trusting its timestamp — every product file mtime is at or before 22:59:48Z (index.test.ts 22:59:48Z, index.ts 22:44:18Z, session-name.ts 22:27:03Z, session-name.test.ts 22:27:23Z). No finding of any severity remains open on this plan.

P-1 CLOSED without a fourth round, which was the point. The fix is the exact assertion I wrote down, applied in place, and I verified it rather than accepting the report: the assertion is present at index.test.ts:283, the targeted suite is 23/23 at bare exit 0 on my own run, and the guard it now witnesses would genuinely go red if deleted. AC4's receipt was re-cited to the post-edit ship gate. Nothing is left open on this plan.
